estimation_procedure.description: Full-sample determinant regression of current-report Fog on the three earnings-change groups. For each cutoff, MBE marks ΔEPS in the interval from zero through 1, 2, or 3 cents; NegEarnChg marks ΔEPS below zero; the baseline group is firms that beat prior-year EPS by more than the cutoff. Columns I–III repeat this specification across the three MBE cutoffs. The authors also report an F test of β1−β2=0 comparing the MBE and NegEarnChg coefficients.

evidence.quote: The regression specification results in three groups in the analysis:

scope.quote: We explore how the readability of annual reports varies with earnings management.
In this paper, we examine whether managers use of complex disclosures goes beyond the presence of “legalese”, but also whether they use complex disclosure to hide information from investors.
Table 4 presents our first test of Hypothesis 1.
The definition of EM in Equation (1) in this analysis is whether a firm met or just beat past year’s earnings.
Panel A presents the results from the full sample.
To address this ambiguity, we repeated our analyses using smaller matched samples, with results shown in Panels B and C of Table 4.

review_notes: Source-first selection: the abstract frames the main question as whether suspected earnings management makes MD&A disclosures harder to read. The authors call Table 4 the first test of H1; Panel A is the full sample and uses MBE cutoffs of 1, 2, and 3 cents. Panels B and C are smaller matched follow-ups that address comparison ambiguity; later accrual/real-management proxies and restatement/misstatement tests are outside this selected family.

The selected equation is the coordinator-verified generic Eq. (1) from the supplied reading derivative. Table 4 supplies the exact RHS terms and MBE thresholds; they were not inferred from the generic control-vector notation. The supplied coordinator note and verified page-tail also confirm that Appendix A’s M&A coding prints “1 otherwise,” the Earnings denominator differs between research-design prose and Appendix A, Size is only called a log, NBSeg/NGSeg are natural logs without a stated +1, and Table 4 refers to Appendix B while this manuscript labels the definitions Appendix A.
The underlying estimator for Table 4 Panel A is not identified. The source reports determinant analyses/regressions and industry-clustered standard errors, but those details do not establish OLS.
results_review_notes: Only the frozen Table 4 Panel A baseline family (Columns I–III) is extracted; later matched-sample, mechanism, placebo, robustness, supplemental and restatement/misstatement tests are outside scope.
Table 2 Panel A provides full-sample descriptives for Fog, retained controls, and raw ΔEPS. MBE and NegEarnChg are not separately summarized there; ΔEPS is retained as their raw input/component.
The source contains unresolved definition issues for Earnings, Size, SpecItems and M&A; printed table values are retained without silently resolving them.
